text:
Ashley Park: dropping a note — saw a bunch of traces starting new roots after gateway -> SQS -> worker. root cause: metadata lost on re-publish path when helpers rebuild messages.
Kevin Liu: are we storing traceparent/tracestate as MessageAttributes or inline in body?
Ashley Park: attributes. example we currently set:
```
MessageAttributes = { "traceparent": { "StringValue": "00-...-...-01" } }
```
Mireille Gomez: SQS keeps attributes but our republish helper `forward_to_dlq()` does `body = json.dumps(event)` and recreates attributes = {} unless explicitly copied. I found it in infra-python `queue_utils.py`.
Samir Patel: that would strip tracing. quick patch is to copy attributes through, but we should standardize a single carrier to avoid per-key mishaps across languages.
Kevin Liu: also `tracestate` with commas and some baggage keys with `=` have broken when clients re-encode. different SDKs end up escaping differently.
Mireille Gomez: propose: write a single attribute `x-redwood-otel` (String) containing base64 of compact JSON like `{ "tp":"traceparent", "ts":"tracestate", "bg":{...}, "sd":"1" }` where `sd` is sampled flag. workers decode and either link or set parent.
Ashley Park: sample human carrier:
```
{"tp":"00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01","ts":"rooney=1","bg":{"uid":"u123"},"sd":"1"}
```
base64 -> `x-redwood-otel` attr.
Kevin Liu: sensible. check SQS limits: attributes + body combined must be <= 256KB; Base64 adds ~33%. tracestate can approach 512 bytes but usually smaller. we should document worst-case and add telemetry on attribute sizes.
Samir Patel: cost note: DLQs and long retention will store that attr for every message. at 5k msg/s it adds up. we should make the carrier minimal and optional per-queue via feature flag `telemetry.preserve_trace_on_queue`.
Mireille Gomez: on processing semantics: should worker start a child span using the incoming traceparent, or start a new root and add incoming as a Link? For async jobs link is more correct and avoids accidental parent-child timing assumptions.
Kevin Liu: agree with Link. Link preserves relationship without implying synchronous causality. collectors/exporters can still reconstruct graph.
Ashley Park: implementation plan from infra side:
- gateway: when publishing to SQS/SNS, set `x-redwood-otel` attr. update `republish()` helper to preserve it.
- SDK helpers (py/go/node): `carrier.decode()` -> returns OpenTelemetry Link + sampling bit.
- worker: start local processing span as root, add Link(s) from decoded carrier.
- add unit + e2e tests for direct publish, DLQ -> republish, SNS fanout.
Samir Patel: PR #3678 created (gateway + python helper). @Mireille please review.
Mireille Gomez: will do. add integration test in `infra/telemetry/tests/test_queue_traces.py` and plan canary in us-west-2 for 24h.
otel-collector-bot: metric `queue.span_links_received` will increment when a worker attaches an external Link. added dashboard tile in telemetry -> traces -> queue-linking.
Ashley Park: follow-ups: Kevin to run attr size audit and add a warning in console when queue carriers exceed 1KB, Samir to publish SDK helpers, Mireille to add migration doc `infra/telemetry/carrier_v0_to_v1.md`.
Kevin Liu: also audit internal HTTP forwards between gateway -> internal-proxy; keep headers + carrier attr so both sync and async paths are covered.
Samir Patel: thumbs up :thumbsup: 
Ashley Park: logs uploaded to `s3://redwood-ops/trace-repro/1934567890/` with sample messages. will start canary Tuesday.
Mireille Gomez: closing here — will open RFC with carrier schema, migration timeline, and opt-out flag. thanks all.
